label: Matt 11:1
text: When Jesus had finished directing his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities.

label: Matt 11:2
text: Now when John heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples

label: Matt 11:3
text: and said to him, “Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?”

label: Matt 11:4
text:
Jesus answered them,
“Go and tell John the things which you hear and see:

label: Matt 11:5
text:
the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear,
the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.

label: Matt 11:6
text: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”

label: Matt 11:7
text:
As these went their way, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John,
“What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

label: Matt 11:8
text: But what did you go out to see? A man in soft clothing? Behold, those who wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

label: Matt 11:9
text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.

label: Matt 11:10
text: For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

label: Matt 11:11
text: Most certainly I tell you, among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.

label: Matt 11:12
text: From the days of John the Baptizer until now, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.

label: Matt 11:13
text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

label: Matt 11:14
text: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.

label: Matt 11:15
text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

label: Matt 11:16
text: “But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call to their companions

label: Matt 11:17
text: and say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned for you, and you didn’t lament.’

label: Matt 11:18
text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’

label: Matt 11:19
text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is justified by her children.”

label: Matt 11:20
text: Then he began to denounce the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they didn’t repent.

label: Matt 11:21
text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

label: Matt 11:22
text: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

label: Matt 11:23
text:
You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades.

For if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in you, it would have remained until today.

label: Matt 11:24
text: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom, on the day of judgment, than for you.”

label: Matt 11:25
text:
At that time, Jesus answered,
“I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.

label: Matt 11:26
text: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.

label: Matt 11:27
text: All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him.

label: Matt 11:28
text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

label: Matt 11:29
text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.

label: Matt 11:30
text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

statement: After directing the Twelve, Jesus went on to teach and preach in their cities - the towns of Galilee.
label: Jesus taught and preached in their cities

statement: John the Baptist was being held in prison when he heard about the works of Christ and sent two of his disciples to Jesus.
label: John the Baptist in prison

statement: Jesus's answer to John lists healings: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them - the language of Isaiah 35:5-6 and 61:1.
label: The healing list in Jesus's reply

statement: Jesus asked the crowds what they went out into the wilderness to see: 'A reed shaken by the wind?'
label: A reed shaken by the wind
note: A modern suggestion that the reed alludes to the reed emblem on Antipas's coinage could not be sourced from a fetched page this run; only the coin motif itself is entered.

statement: Those who wear soft clothing are in kings' houses - soft raiment marks royal palaces, not the wilderness prophet.
label: Soft raiment in kings' houses

statement: Jesus applied to John the written promise 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you' (Malachi 3:1).
label: The messenger quotation (Malachi 3:1)

statement: Jesus called John 'Elijah, who is to come', invoking the first-century expectation that Elijah would return before the day of the Lord.
label: Elijah who is to come

statement: Children sat in the marketplaces calling to their companions with wedding and funeral games: 'We played the flute for you, and you didn't dance. We mourned for you, and you didn't lament.'
label: Children in the marketplaces

statement: Opponents called the Son of Man 'a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners' - the charge formula of Deuteronomy 21:20.
label: Glutton and drunkard, friend of tax collectors

statement: Chorazin was a Galilean town on the Korazim Plateau above the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee, denounced in the woes for not repenting.
label: Woe to Chorazin

statement: Bethsaida was a town of the period near the Sea of Galilee, denounced in the woes for not repenting.
label: Woe to Bethsaida

statement: Tyre and Sidon stood as Phoenician cities of the Roman period, known to Galilean audiences and remembered as objects of judgment.
label: Tyre and Sidon

statement: Capernaum, where most of Jesus's mighty works were done, was denounced: 'You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades.'
label: Capernaum exalted to heaven

statement: The land of Sodom was remembered as judged by God; its day would be more tolerable than Capernaum's.
label: The land of Sodom on the day of judgment

statement: Jesus used the yoke - the wooden farm implement and, in rabbinic idiom, a metaphor of discipleship - to describe his teaching: 'my yoke is easy'.
label: Take my yoke upon you
